cards.claim: Under budget restrictions, importance sampling approaches do not provide consistent improvement over uniform sampling
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10/100, budget-restricted iterative training (e.g., 30% budget reduction)
cards.effect: No consistent improvement; uniform sampling is as good or better
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from comparative experiments on CIFAR-10/100
cards.quote: We show that under budget restrictions, importance sampling approaches do not provide a consistent improvement over uniform sampling.

cards.claim: RICAP data augmentation maintains accuracy when budget is reduced to 30% on CIFAR-10/100
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10/100, 30% budget reduction, RICAP data augmentation applied
cards.effect: Accuracy is maintained (specific magnitude not stated in abstract)
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison on CIFAR-10/100 under budget constraints
cards.quote: when reducing the budget to a 30% in CIFAR-10/100, RICAP data augmentation maintains accuracy, while importance sampling does not.

cards.claim: Under budget restrictions, introducing adequate data augmentation is more effective than importance sampling for maintaining accuracy
cards.conditions: Deep neural networks under budget constraints (e.g., 30% budget reduction on CIFAR-10/100)
cards.effect: Maintains or recovers accuracy more effectively than sample-importance approaches
cards.evidence: Empirical finding from comparison of augmentation vs. importance sampling strategies
cards.quote: We suggest that, given a specific budget, the best course of action is to disregard the importance and introduce adequate data augmentation

cards.claim: DNNs under budget restrictions benefit from variety in the training set more than from optimal sample selection
cards.conditions: Budget-constrained DNN training, balancing high performance with low computational requirements
cards.effect: Variety in training set is more effective for performance than finding the 'right' samples to train on
cards.evidence: Conclusion from empirical work comparing sampling strategies vs. augmentation/diversity
cards.quote: DNNs under budget restrictions benefit greatly from variety in the training set and that finding the right samples to train on is not the most effective strategy when balancing high performance with low computational requirements.
